title: Article 68 — Time of holding election to fill vacancy in the office of Vice-President and the term of office of person elected to fill casual vacancy

content.overview: Article 68 provides that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of Vice-President shall be completed before the expiration of the term. An election to fill a vacancy occurring by reason of death, resignation or removal or otherwise shall be held as soon as possible after the occurrence of the vacancy. The person elected to fill a casual vacancy is entitled to hold office for the full term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
content.glance: Term-end vacancy: election before term expires. Casual vacancy: as soon as possible. Casual-vacancy VP gets full 5-year term.
content.study:
Article 68 parallels Article 62 for the Vice-President. Ordinary vacancy: election before term ends. Casual vacancy: as soon as possible (no express 6-month outer limit in the same terms as Art 62). Casual-vacancy successor holds a full five-year term.

Examination: pre-term-end election; casual vacancy timing; full term for successor.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Expiration of term: election completed before term ends.
2. Casual vacancy: election as soon as possible after occurrence.
3. Casual-vacancy VP: full 5-year term from entering office.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must a Vice-Presidential election be held?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy caused by expiration of the term of Vice-President must be completed before the term expires. An election to fill a casual vacancy must be held as soon as possible after the vacancy. A person elected to fill a casual vacancy holds office for a full term of five years from entering upon office.

examTips: Parallel to Art 62; full term for casual-vacancy VP.

keyTakeaways: Art 68: timing of VP elections; full term for casual vacancy.
